Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
111 PM PST Fri Nov 27 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Mild temperatures will continue through Sunday morning. 

* A 20-30% chance for showers along the Oregon border arrives late 
  tonight into early Saturday morning. 

* Strong gusty winds arrive Sunday morning through Monday morning 
  ahead of an incoming storm. Valley rain and mountain snow arrive 
  Sunday and will linger into early Wednesday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

A stretch of mild weather with cloud cover will be with us through 
the bulk of the weekend. We cannot rule out a shower passing to the 
north, along the Oregon border, where a 20-30% chance for showers  
this evening. This brush-by system will also kick up winds along 
the Sierra, with gusts of 55-65 mph this evening into Saturday 
morning. Our mild temperatures will range the mid-50s to lower 60s
through the weekend, although some cooling will impact 
northeastern California and the northern Sierra on Sunday ahead of
an incoming system. 

The incoming system will feature gusty winds that will bring choppy 
lake waters to Lake Tahoe and Pyramid Lake as early as Sunday 
morning. Winds across Sierra ridges will gust as high as 80+ mph, 
while gusts across valleys could reach 40-45 mph. Precipitation will 
arrive to the Sierra midday Sunday, with rain below 8000-8500 
feet and snow above. Snow levels will take a tumble overnight 
Sunday into Monday, bringing snow lines down to as low as 6500 
feet for northeastern California, and down to 7000-7500 for the 
Tahoe Basin and south along the Sierra. Spillover into western
Nevada will be limited with the initial wave Sunday into Monday. 
Even though amounts will be a bit lighter than recent storms, keep
winter driving in mind if your travels will bring you above snow 
levels. Check in with the latest road conditions and keep your 
vehicle winter ready before you need to travel.

By Tuesday morning, northeastern California will see snow levels 
down to 5000-5500 feet as a reinforcing second low drops in from the 
northern Pacific. Snow levels for the Tahoe Basin may drop to around 
6000-6500 feet, which would start to mix some wet snowflakes into 
the rainfall. Snow amounts should remain on the lighter side, with 
the highest peaks along the Sierra receiving up to 18 inches of new 
snow. Accumulations around lake level will likely be limited to 
elevated surfaces such as vehicles and elevated walkways, with 
wet roads. Up on Mt. Rose, we could see 6-10 inches of snow (high 
end has a 20% chance), while Virginia City could see 1-3 inches 
(high end has a 10% chance). The recent track that guidance has 
offered wants to send the center of circulation to the southern 
end of the Sierra, which would work to limit available moisture to
the north, generally from the Tahoe Basin to the northern Sierra.

Our confidence in the second system is gaining ground, but since 
the recent model solutions have a trend of disagreement in the 
longer range output, we will reserve judgment on storms beyond the
Tuesday system. Timing, positioning and magnitude have all 
disagreed beyond the short term, so we will await clarification. 
HRICH

&&

.AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast: 

* VFR conditions with light winds and widespread high level
  clouds, followed by a thicker mid-high level cloud deck this
  afternoon through Saturday. Valley inversions may produce minor
  slantwise visibility reductions Saturday morning. Increasing
  west FL100 winds (gusts to 55 kt) may bring increased 
  turbulence and periods of LLWS this evening and overnight. 

Regional Outlook: 

* VFR for all main terminals, except patchy FZFG chances (less
  than 20%) Saturday morning at KTRK. Increasing FL100 winds
  (gusts to 55 kt) move into the area tonight, bringing increased
  turbulence and periods of LLWS for all main terminals. Valley 
  inversions may produce minor slantwise visibility reductions 
  this morning for KCXP/KMEV. 
  
24-72 Hour Outlook: 

* VFR conditions with widespread mid-high level cloud cover and
  light surface winds continue. West FL100 winds increase while 
  shifting to SW late Saturday night through Sunday night with 
  turbulence and LLWS potential returning. Surface winds also 
  increase at all sites Sunday afternoon-night, with periods of 
  rain (and even a 15% chance for lightning) with MVFR/brief IFR 
  for KTRK-KTVL, while other sites have a lower 30-50% chance of 
  lighter rain showers Sunday evening and overnight. 
  
MJD/McKellar
